creator: Shivam Gupta
notes: Final narrated demo assembled from actual Chrome Page.screencastFrame captures on the hosted Firebase app. Capture timestamp differences are preserved at normal speed; static final frames hold through the recorded elapsed time. Fictional example. Narration timing comes from final WAV samples.

scenes.title: Home from hospital. One result is still pending.

captions.text: Anita is home from hospital. Her daughter, Maya, has the discharge notes.
But one result is still pending. Who will make sure somebody follows it through?

actions: Hold on the fictional care board with the pending blood culture visible.
proof: The Anita/Maya example is visibly fictional.

scenes.title: The next step, accounted for.

captions.text: This is Looplight, a follow-up ledger by Shivam Gupta.
It turns the next steps already written in discharge notes into a plan people can inspect and track.

actions: Open one care-board task and briefly show its source sentence.
proof: The source sentence and task are visible together.

scenes.title: Start with the original instructions.

captions.text: Start with Anita's fictional example. Open the source, then find the open loops.
A small trained text model and explicit rules suggest follow-up items.
Nothing becomes a confirmed task until someone checks it.

actions: Open Add discharge notes.
Select Anita's discharge.
Choose Find the open loops.
Hold on the resulting Needs review items.
proof: Show the actual analysis action and its result in one continuous take.

scenes.title: Keep the source and the uncertainty.

captions.text: Open the pending blood culture result. Its exact source sentence stays attached.
Missing timing appears as a question for the care team, so an unclear instruction stays visibly unresolved.

actions: Open the pending result through Check details.
Pause on source evidence.
Show missing timing and the suggested question.
proof: No date has been invented for the pending result.

scenes.title: Review what the system missed.

captions.text: A convincing task list can still miss something.
The original document remains reviewable sentence by sentence, including text the system did not turn into tasks.
Add a missed follow-up from its original sentence.

actions: Open Source documents and a sentence without a proposed task.
Use Add a missed follow-up.
Keep the source wording and choose Add for review.
Show the new item needing review.
proof: Show an actual manual addition with its source still attached.

scenes.title: Name the person tracking the next step.

captions.text: Now name Maya as the person tracking the result, review the details, and confirm the follow-up.
Maya is tracking the next step. The app does not assign her clinical responsibility.

actions: Return to the blood culture task.
Fill the named tracker field with Maya (daughter).
Choose Confirm this follow-up.
Hold on the confirmed state.
proof: Capture the confirmation click and resulting state.

scenes.title: A result arriving is one step.

captions.text: Here is the important distinction. Record that the result has arrived.
The task stays open because receipt and clinician review are separate steps.
A file arriving does not tell the family what happens next.

actions: Open Record progress.
Enter a short fictional receipt note.
Choose Record result received.
Hold on Result received and outstanding clinician review.
proof: Receipt must not produce reported completion.

scenes.title: Give the follow-up a recorded ending.

captions.text: After a conversation with the clinician, record who reviewed the result and what they said.
Confirm that this is your report, then record completion.
The history preserves a user-reported ending, not independent proof of clinical review.

actions: Enter Dr. Rao (fictional clinician) and a clearly fictional outcome note.
Select the user-report confirmation.
Choose Record completion.
Open History and pause on the recorded ending.
proof: Show named clinician, outcome, acknowledgement, and completion.
Do not imply a verified clinician signed the record.

scenes.title: A plan people can bring with them.

captions.text: Take the plan to the next conversation. The visit brief keeps follow-ups and source text together.
Calendar entries use confirmed dates.
In a signed-in care space, create a plan and refresh: the saved plan returns.

actions: Open Visit brief and show the source beside each next step.
Export Calendar file and show the download confirmation.
Cut to an already signed-in care space.
Create or import a fictional plan within that space.
Refresh and show the same saved plan returning.
proof: Do not imply anonymous demo changes transfer through sign-in.
Persistence claim requires the final Firebase implementation to pass refresh QA.

scenes.title: A focused first customer.

captions.text: The first customer to test is a primary-care or transitions coordinator already chasing discharge follow-up.
The starting price hypothesis is one hundred and forty-nine dollars a month, for one hundred episodes.
A supervised pilot must test preparation time and correction burden.

actions: Hold on the final plan, or use the supplied editorial business card.
Keep the words Pricing hypothesis visible.
proof: No revenue, customer adoption, or measured savings claim.

media.body:
Pricing hypothesis
One coordinator account
Pilot measures preparation time and correction burden

scenes.title: A useful prototype, with visible limits.

captions.text: Looplight is a working prototype evaluated on synthetic examples.
It can miss instructions and needs human review.
It does not diagnose, interpret a result, or demonstrate a proven health benefit.

actions: Show the final Evidence & AI screen with the synthetic-data caveat.
Do not zoom into numerical results unless they match the final release report.
proof: No clinical validation or autonomous safety claim.

scenes.title: Every next step has a recorded ending.

captions.text: Shivam Gupta built Looplight with AI-assisted development.
Every next step has a source, a person tracking it, and a recorded ending.
That is the work Looplight helps make visible.

actions: Return to the actual completed follow-up and visible history.
Hold a clean final frame for at least two seconds.
proof: Credit Shivam as project builder without inventing specific personal coding work.
